x: At 5 miles Sheffield lost Allen and Highgate got their noses in front, only to lose Howell and Meadows which put them right back and Woodford came through with a strong challenge to Sheffield who had also lost Holland.
Portsmouth who had been behind us for some time were getting ominously near, for Meadows on this leg put up the best time of the day,and were at this point a mere nineteen seconds behind us.
By a remarkable coincidence they finished 5 in 37, exactly as in 1966, but this time their sixth man (Meadows) was 102nd against the previous year's 173rd.

It was generally felt that Coventry and Portsmouth were the main teams to watch so although Hammond brought Godiva home with a useful lead it was gratifying to see Geoff hold Meadows of Portsmouth to one second.
John held his form well and, although 12th, was only 36 seconds behind the leader. Coventry ominously, were second, Derby 5th, Manchester 14th and Portsmouth (Meadows) a disastrous 21st.
